about: Inputs of the worked example in Section 3.4 of the manuscript: mobile primary-care clinics for three Oklahoma towns in 2030. Status is one of: published, calculated in screening.py, planning assumption, or stakeholder requirement.

us_population.source: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024) World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant, total population of the United States of America

towns.unit: persons; population_2025 on 1 July 2025 and estimates_base_2020 on 1 April 2020
towns.source: U.S. Census Bureau (2026) QuickFacts, Vintage 2025: Population estimates, July 1, 2025, and Population estimates base, April 1, 2020

visit_rate.unit: visits to primary-care physicians per person per year, 2019
visit_rate.source: Santo L, Kang K (2023) National Ambulatory Medical Care Survey: 2019 national summary tables, Table 1: 161.4 visits per 100 people (standard error 9.5)

z_95.status: statistical constant for a 95 percent range

mobile_share.unit: share of primary-care visits that stakeholders assign to the mobile clinics

median_annual_visits_per_clinic.unit: visits per mobile clinic per year
median_annual_visits_per_clinic.source: Malone NC et al. (2020) Mobile health clinics in the United States. Int J Equity Health 19:40

mean_annual_cost_primary_care_clinic.unit: dollars per primary-care mobile clinic per year (58 clinics reported cost)
mean_annual_cost_primary_care_clinic.source: Malone NC et al. (2020) Mobile health clinics in the United States. Int J Equity Health 19:40

service_days_per_week.unit: service days of each van per week

vans_per_town.status: candidate set: a fifth van raises the monthly cost above the budget
